title: PPA search manifest v1
description: What a search run published. The shape exists so that two searches can be compared on more than a trial count: every budget dimension, every trial in every terminal state, and a NAMED reason for each candidate that was not comparable. A manifest that satisfies this schema is well-formed; programs/ppa_search_run.py --verify additionally checks that it is self-consistent, which is a different and stronger question.

schema.description: First key of every instance document (PPA_INTERFACES section 5).

space_digest.description: sha256: of the search space this run drew from, through _ppa/canonical_json. Two manifests are only comparable when this matches; different spaces are different searches.

budget.description: Every budget dimension, declared. A field left out is not a default, it is an unanswered question, so all ten are required and an unbounded one is stated as null.

max_trials.description: 1 is a legitimate budget and produces a complete bundle of one point. 0 is not a budget.

max_full_pnr_trials.description: A SUBSET of max_trials, not an extra allowance. Separate from the trial count because 50 synthesis trials and 50 routed trials are not the same work.

failed_trial_policy.description: Whether a crashed trial spends budget. Both answers are defensible and they give different trial counts, so it may not be left implicit.

seed.description: The candidate sequence is a seeded shuffle. Same space + same seed + same budget reproduces the same sequence.

cache_policy.description: A cache hit costs no CPU. Under REUSE the manifest must also say how many trials were hits, or the published CPU-hours describe a different amount of work than a reader assumes.

budget_spent.description: What the budget actually bought. Derived from the candidate states, never incremented by hand: a counter and a list can disagree, a derived count cannot.

cpu_hours.description: null, never 0.0, when no trial reported CPU time: 'not instrumented' and 'used no CPU' are opposite facts and 0.0 reads as the second.

wall_seconds.description: null when the elapsed span cannot be reconstructed (concurrency > 1 without timestamps). Dividing a sum by the concurrency would publish a model as a measurement.

states.description: Count per lifecycle state. Present for every state including the zeroes, so a state that never occurred and a state nobody tracked are distinguishable.

fidelity_ladder.description: The ordered stage vocabulary, cheapest first. Published with the manifest so a reader can rank completed_stage without importing this plugin.

feasibility_terms.description: Every component of the eligibility verdict, named individually so a verdict built from a subset is visibly a subset. Detailed-route DRC alone is one of these terms.

lever_notes.description: One entry per admitted lever this run did NOT vary, and why. A lever that silently vanished from a search and a lever that was never searchable must not look the same in the artefact.

candidates.description: EVERY candidate ever proposed, in every terminal state, including the ones that never ran. Publishing only the winner makes a lucky draw look like a method.

identity.description: sha256 of (space digest, knobs) through the one serializer, so a cache hit is checkable rather than asserted.

state.description: Terminal states only. PROPOSED and RUNNING are deliberately absent: an unfinished trial published as a result is a measurement that has not happened yet.

completed_stage.description: The highest ladder rung this trial actually reached. NEVER an integer: a tuner iteration counter (ORFS/Ray Tune `step`) counts objective reports, not flow progress, and the same value can mean 'died in floorplan' and 'finished routing'. The type here refuses it.

verdict.description: UNDETERMINED is its own answer and never folds into INELIGIBLE: 'we checked and it fails' and 'we never checked' are different findings.

terms.description: Per-term status. An ELIGIBLE verdict whose terms are not all PASS or NOT_APPLICABLE is an eligibility claim on a partial vector.

frontier_input.description: What the Pareto lane is allowed to see, and a named reason for every candidate left out. An empty included[] is a legitimate complete answer: the budget bought no comparable point.

frontier_stage.description: The single scope the whole frontier is taken at. Fixed, because a frontier mixing stages is a category error with a plot.

what_the_budget_bought.description: The trial count with CPU-hours and wall time in the same breath, because the number a reader takes away is whichever is easiest to read.
